reader.requirement: At --std 85, when any file-name-4 of a MERGE GIVING phrase is an indexed file, the MERGE must be refused unless the first KEY data-name is under ASCENDING and occupies exactly the character positions (offset and length) in the sort-merge record that the prime record key occupies in that file's record; a MERGE whose GIVING files are not indexed is unconstrained by the rule.
reader.edition-search: grep of Edition.Edition, DialectLevel, Year <, CobolVersion, Dialect in SortBinder.cs, SortKeyAdmission.cs and RecordLayout.cs: the only consults are SortBinder#BindRelease (DialectLevel < 2002, RELEASE range outcome) and SortBinder#ScreenSameClauses (held1985, SORT GIVING in SAME RECORD AREA); neither is on the BindMerge -> ScreenIndexedGivingKey path, which is edition-neutral
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the 1985 'same character positions' and the 2023 'same byte positions' ask one offset-and-length comparison, and the screen runs identically at --std 85 and --std 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises only a DESCENDING first key; not exercised by it: an ASCENDING first key at a different offset or length, several GIVING files with one indexed, a DESCENDING first key followed by an ascending one, a variable-occurrence SD record, and the admitted forms

probes.expected: admitted (ASCENDING SA at bytes 1..2 = prime key IK 1..2, sequential access); records written in key order
admitted with ACCESS DYNAMIC and a DESCENDING minor key
admitted: GIVING sequential G2 and indexed G1

probes.printed: error COBOL1757: MERGE GIVING file 'G1' is an indexed file ... associated with a DESCENDING phrase

probes.expected: refused: the FIRST data-name-1 is under DESCENDING even though a later one is ASCENDING

probes.printed: error COBOL1757 ... first key occupies bytes 1..2 ... prime record key 'IK' occupies bytes 3..4

probes.expected: refused: only the second key matches the prime key's positions
refused: the indexed one of two GIVING files
admitted: SD record with OCCURS DEPENDING ON after the key; key at 1..2
refused: the ODO count item is the first key

citations.check: OK  §1985:XI.4.1.3 SR10  (4.1.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR10

reader.notes: ScreenIndexedGivingKey compares the first key's (offset, length) in the SD record to the prime key's window in each indexed GIVING file and refuses a DESCENDING first key; it is the same code at every edition and needs no 1985 arm because the 1985 rule is the same comparison. Every refusal and admission probed at --std 85 matched the text; the refusal cites §2023:14.9.24.3 SR10 in its message.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:XI.4.1.3 SR10 and SortBinder.cs#ScreenIndexedGivingKey (keys[0] Descending check, then PrimeKeyBytes window vs first key offset/length via RecordLayout.KeyWindowOf with each key's own root). Probes at --std 85 aimed at multiple record descriptions: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/sample-shared/out/refute-1985-08/r2-sd-second-rec.cob (key SA OF SR2, the SD's second record, at 1..2; RECORD KEY IK OF G1S, the indexed file's second record, at 1..2) -> ran, 01ZZ01/02XX02/03YY03; E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/sample-shared/out/refute-1985-08/r2-sd-second-bad.cob (key SB OF SR2 at 3..4) -> COBOL1757 'first key occupies bytes 3..4 ... prime record key IK occupies bytes 1..2'. cite.py: 'OK §1985:XI.4.1.3 SR10 (4.1.3 Syntax Rules) the text is in SR10'.
